subject: Sunridge RFP: Disaster Recovery sequencing & failback procedures
messages:
From: Oliver Jensen <ojensen@sunridge.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@sunridge.com, IT-SG Team <it@sunridge.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T14:03:00Z
Subject: RFP - DR sequencing, RTO/RPO clarifications

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick intake call earlier. As we prepare Sunridge's RFP pack, the evaluation committee requested more granularity on two items before the pricing stage:

1) Exact failover and failback sequencing for a regional outage (us-east1 -> us-west1). They want steps, time estimates, and automated/manual gates.
2) Confirmed achievable RTO/RPO targets for our common deployment pattern (dedicated pool + prefix caching) and how those change if KV cache warmup is required.

I've attached the DR questionnaire (Sunridge_DRQ_v2.pdf). Can you confirm if Redwood can meet: 
- RTO: <= 5 minutes for control plane + <= 30 minutes for full KV cache warmup (best-effort)
- RPO: <= 1 minute for in-flight request persistence

If possible, please provide a short runbook excerpt that we can share with our GRC team.

Oliver
Oliver Jensen
Head of Platform Risk | Sunridge Financial Services
ojensen@sunridge.com

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Jensen <ojensen@sunridge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T18:20:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP - DR sequencing, RTO/RPO clarifications

Hi Oliver — appreciate the clear ask and the questionnaire. High-level answers up front:

- Control-plane failover RTO: typically under 90s (automated leader election + warmed control cache).
- Data-plane availability (ability to serve live inference): dependent on KV-cache warm state. With prefix caching and active cross-region replication in Dedicated, we target RTO <= 5 min for functional traffic (best-effort warm) and full model-KV parity within 20-45 minutes depending on sequence length distribution.
- RPO: We persist request metadata and checkpoints to durable storage and maintain near-synchronous metadata replication; operationally we aim for <= 30s in the common Dedicated config; 1 minute is achievable in our higher-tier replication mode.

Attached is a concise runbook excerpt (redwood-failback-runbook.docx) and a short answers doc embedded in the attached PDF. For the committee, I've summarized an ordered failover/failback sequence below — I'll also attach a sanitized excerpt for your GRC team.

Failover (us-east1 -> us-west1) - condensed sequence:
1) Detection & validation (automated): health probes flag region; control-plane alerts generated.
2) Automated routing change: Smart routing moves new requests to us-west1 based on policy (seconds).
3) Capacity allocation: Dedicated pool in us-west1 scales to pre-warmed commit (if burst config enabled) — typically 1-3 minutes.
4) KV prefix fallback: requests hit cold cache and stream from durable store; degraded latency until cache warms.
5) Optional manual gating: customers can choose to hold non-critical queues via console.

Failback (us-west1 -> us-east1) - condensed sequence:
1) Validate health and reachability in origin region.
2) Gradual traffic shift with canary percentage routing (10% -> 50% -> 100%) to monitor quality and latency.
3) Accelerated cache pre-warm using snapshot/replication APIs if customers opt in.

I'm cc'ing Laura and Marcus for technical confirmation on the numbers (they'll expand where needed). Are you ok if we send the sanitized runbook to GRC and include a short appendix on warmup timelines by model family?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP - DR sequencing, RTO/RPO clarifications

Aditya — quick internal notes to confirm precise numbers we should present to Sunridge:

- Control plane failover: we can confidently state <120s under normal load (with automatic leader election + replicated control state).
- Data-plane (functional serving) RTO: for Dedicated with cross-region replication + prefix caching enabled, state we can commit to in the RFP: 5 minutes (best-effort), with a note: "dependent on client cache size and sequence distribution; bulk-warm can be done in parallel to accelerate to sub-10 minute full parity for typical workloads."
- RPO: state we can commit: <= 30s on the standard replication tier; <= 60s on lower-cost async mode. 1 minute (<=60s) should be included as an explicit contractual option for higher-tier customers.

Attachment suggestion: include a short table (model-size vs warmup window) and an action matrix that maps detection state -> automated/manual steps. Marcus, can you add the matrix and an example traffic-shift timeline (10/50/100) with sample latency hit numbers?

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: RFP - DR sequencing, RTO/RPO clarifications

Hi Oliver — attaching the sanitized runbook and our short answers for the RFP (see attachments). Key contractual commitments we propose for the RFP packet:

- Control-plane failover RTO: < 120s (automated).
- Data-plane functional RTO: target 5 minutes for Dedicated with cross-region replication + prefix caching enabled (best-effort); provide an optional "accelerated warm" add-on to guarantee sub-10-minute full parity.
- RPO: standard replication tier <= 30s; premium replication tier <= 60s (explicitly called out as the on-contract option to meet <= 1 minute requirement).

Action items for Sunridge: please confirm which replication tier you prefer for the committed nodes (standard vs premium) and whether you will opt into accelerated warm snapshots during failback. Once you confirm, we'll return an amended SLT section for inclusion in the redlines.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short 20m call to walk through the runbook with GRC.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
